physics_goals.locator: E158 site, main page 'About the experiment'
physics_goals.quote: A comprehensive search for physics beyond the standard model is incomplete unless equally sensitive measurements are carried out both on and off the Z0 resonance.
physics_goals.value: Measure the weak mixing angle at low momentum transfer through the parity-violating asymmetry in electron-electron (Moller) scattering, testing the electroweak theory off the Z pole and probing physics beyond the Standard Model at the TeV scale

summary.plain: E158 fired a 45 to 48 GeV spin-polarised electron beam into liquid hydrogen at SLAC and measured the tiny difference in scattering from the target's electrons between the two spin directions. It gave the weak mixing angle at low energy and showed that it changes with energy as the Standard Model predicts.
summary.technical: Parity-violating Moller (e-e) scattering in End Station A: 45 and 48 GeV longitudinally polarised electrons on a 1.57 m liquid-hydrogen target, Moller electrons of 13-24 GeV selected by a magnetic spectrometer and integrated 60 m downstream in a copper/fused-silica-fibre calorimeter; three runs in 2002-2003; A_PV = -131 +- 14 +- 10 ppb, sin^2 theta_W^eff = 0.2397 +- 0.0010 +- 0.0008 at Q^2 = 0.026 GeV^2, running of the weak mixing angle observed at over 6 sigma.
